previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old male with a history of quadriplegia, tracheostomy, GJ tube, and chronic Foley catheter was admitted from his nursing home for altered mental status and hypotension. He was found to have hyperkalemia with peaked T waves, acute kidney injury likely due to obstructive uropathy, and hospital-acquired and aspiration pneumonia. He received emergency treatment for hyperkalemia and was started on IV cefepime and linezolid. His Foley catheter was replaced, draining 1.8 liters, and his renal function improved. Sputum culture grew Proteus mirabilis, sensitive to cefepime. Infectious disease recommended completing 8 days of cefepime. The patient refused a PICC line, so he remained hospitalized to complete IV therapy. His warfarin was held due to elevated INR, then restarted at 5 mg daily with bridging enoxaparin due to subtherapeutic levels. Chronic pain from pressure ulcers was managed with increased PRN morphine and palliative care consultation. He was discharged to extended care with instructions to continue antibiotics orally, manage pain, monitor INR, and follow up on electrolytes and vitamin D.
